metadata.title: A structural obstruction to (1,1,3,3,4)-packing colorings
metadata.description: Mortada, El Zein and Al Hajjar asked whether every connected claw-free subcubic graph, apart from their specified exception, admits a (1,1,3,3,4)-packing coloring. We give a negative answer. For every odd integer k >= 3, the triangle expansion of a ring of k diamonds is a connected cubic graph on 12k vertices that admits no such coloring. The proof selects an arbitrary existing high-colored vertex in each triangle. The selected labels give a proper three-coloring of the core, and the radius-four class forces an external private neighbor at each of its core vertices. This requirement excludes that class from every diamond tip, leaving an impossible two-coloring of an odd cycle. The proof is structural and requires no exhaustive search. A 36-vertex member is also certified in Lean using actual graph distances; that formalization does not cover the entire infinite family.
